caption: I planned for R3 000 left and ended with R400. Which line always betrays your budget?

slides.title:
I budgeted my R22 300
p/m salary.
Then I checked.
Living in Roodepoort
slides.body:
Female, 26
Single, no kids
Job: Articled accountant
Net salary: R22 300 p/m

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: Room in a 2 bed flat, water, wifi
slides.body: Budgeted R6 500. Spent R6 500. This is the only line where the plan survived.

slides.title: Car instalment
slides.body: Budgeted R3 100. Spent R3 100. The car is not the problem.

slides.title: Eating out
slides.includes: Work lunches, weekends, delivery when I'm tired
slides.body: Budgeted R1 500. Spent R3 200. I had to read that number twice.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Checkers, plus the Woolies treats that aren't groceries
slides.body: Budgeted R2 000. The extra R400 was all snacks.

slides.title: Clothes & online shopping
slides.includes: Shein, Zara sale, two returns I never did
slides.body: Budgeted R800. One bad Friday and a courier with my name on it.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Medical aid R1 100, Petrol R1 100, Car insurance R650, Phone R450, Black tax R800, Stokvel R300, Funeral policy R150
slides.body: These were all on budget. The overspending came from the lines I pretended were small.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R22 300. I planned to have R3 000 left. I have R400.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I imported my actuals from my statement into Beyond Horizon and put them next to my budget.

The gap on eating out and shopping was R3 050.

No bank login needed.
